title: Why do airplane windows have tiny holes?

lines.text: Have you ever noticed that tiny pinhole at the bottom of commercial airplane windows?
lines.caps: Why do airplane *windows | have a tiny *hole?

lines.text: It is not a manufacturing defect; that tiny hole is a critical lifesaving safety feature.
lines.caps: That tiny hole is a *lifesaving | safety *feature!

lines.text: Airplane passenger windows consist of three separate acrylic panes.
At thirty-five thousand feet, the air pressure outside is dramatically lower than inside the pressurized cabin.
lines.caps: Extreme pressure difference | between inside and *outside

lines.text: The tiny hole, called a bleed valve, balances air pressure between the middle pane and the outer pane.
lines.caps: The bleed hole *balances | pressure between the *panes

lines.text: This forces the tough outer pane to carry all cabin pressurization stress, keeping the inner pane safe.
lines.caps: Forces the thick *outer pane | to carry all the *stress

lines.text: It also vents moisture to prevent your window from frosting over during flight.
